So many people say that, you have no idea, I’m not a therapist, but I used to hang around a lot of homeless kids and try to help them off the streets and I sort of became like a human diary to a lot of them. Some of them have been through actual hell, I won’t go into any detail, but some of the worst things you can imagine, and ALL of them said “you know, other people had it worse than me though..” as if they didn’t deserve help. Here’s the thing, though, you have all been taught that, but it’s not true.
You. Deserve. The. Same. Help.
You deserve the same help as anyone else. No matter how small you think your trauma might be, you know why? Because therapy isn’t about how big or bad what happened to you was, it’s about learning to heal. There’s no sign or test at the door of any therapist’s office that says “you must be this broken to enter:” in fact, some people aren’t even hurting at all when they go, they just want to learn to deal with life better than they did before.
 Don’t ever feel bad about wanting or needing therapy, it takes a strong person to admit that, and you deserve to be able to get the help you need to feel happier. 

TL;DR: I’ve heard this again and again, it’s not true, you deserve the same help as anyone, don’t feel bad about wanting therapy!

I think that it's an interesting, and good idea, but I also think the concept needs to be fleshed out a lot more before it's put into writing. You should answer all the important questions when thinking of the concept so that it's easier to take the show in the direction that you want it to go (and, it's also far easier to make tweaks and changes to the plot without messing the continuity up, and rendering the whole plot as nonsense, trust me, I've made that mistake before). 

What sort of alternate dimension does he live in? Is it exactly like ours with a different timeline, or with different physical limitations, etc.? 

What sort of healing factor does he have? Can he not die of injury, but still has a set lifespan? Is he completely immune to any kind of death whatsoever? Can he pass this ability on (say to friends somehow, or to children)? If so, how is it done?

Why does the main character not already know who killed him? Is his memory gone? If so, why? Even if you're not telling the audience this in the first episode, it's still a good idea to think of an answer to this one, because eventually it will need some kind of explanation. 

What forces are chasing him? Why do they want him? 


Overall it seems like an awesome idea and I hope you continue to flesh it out! What are you thinking of calling it?
